scope: source-grounded authoring cards; not runtime verification

rooms.question: Does softness belong only to the falling body?
rooms.ontology: A deformation encounter depends on body shape,material parameters,contact geometry and the conditions of release.
rooms.action: Compare the labelled Bouncy Collider and Slippery Collider stations,then a torus or corner-strike specimen. Look for what the setup changes before explaining the resulting pose.
rooms.observable: Different contact arrangements produce different motions and settled shapes; labels identify the intended comparison.
rooms.mechanism: gallery_part2 selects tests13–24; bouncy sets collider bounce1,slippery sets friction0 on a ramp,other tests change body shape,drop offset,drag,pressure or stiffness.
rooms.limit: This is not a controlled single-variable series: some neighbours change several properties. A label describes configuration,not a measured result.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Select two stations with the same body and release,changing only collider friction,then preserve their starting pose as a reference.

sources.fact: 224–333 test13–24 configurations;449 selection by gallery_part;create_test_cell constructs bodies/colliders.

rooms.question: If a body stops changing, has it reached equilibrium or has somebody stopped the experiment?
rooms.ontology: A simulation state and the decision to halt or heavily damp its updates are distinct.
rooms.action: Compare the four soft bodies and their remaining motion; look for differences between forms arrested at different times.
rooms.observable: Four bodies are released in a2×2 arrangement and receive stopping interventions on separate timers.
rooms.mechanism: _on_stop_timeout calls stop_soft_body,sets process disabled,damping100 and stiffness1; restart restores processing and stiffness0.5.
rooms.limit: This is not a pinned cloth sheet,despite the room title. Heavy damping and changed stiffness do not constitute an exact snapshot or evidence of natural rest.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Restore a real pinned cloth comparison here,or add a clock and start-pose witness to distinguish stopping a simulation from material relaxation.
rooms.cautions: Source read only; actual museum runtime, reachability, controls and learner understanding remain unverified. Intended cloth lesson remains core_gap. No cloth present and no verified VR stop controls; do not promote mismatch as a proof about cloth.
rooms.core_gap: Current primary is timed soft-body stopping; it is not pinned cloth.
rooms.smallest_repair_candidate: Restore a working cloth sheet with pins/supports and one clear stiffness orrelease comparison.

rooms.question: When the shape yields, what does its colour tell you?
rooms.ontology: A measurement overlay expresses a chosen quantity about deformation; the same body can support several readings.
rooms.action: Compare the resting outline with the changing heatmap; use MODE to compare strain,collision andvolume readings,then vary STIFFNESS while leaving other controls alone.
rooms.observable: The specimen deforms while overlays and labels emphasise different aspects of its state.
rooms.mechanism: Harness delegates to rounded_softbody; its controls create STIFFNESS/PRESSURE/SQUEEZE/MODE. Strain-like value uses displacement from captured rest points and a running maximum for colour normalisation. In _process, Volume mode also calls _apply_volume_correction, which adjusts pressure in response to volume error; modes do not all preserve dynamics.
rooms.limit: Colour is a selected diagnostic,not pain or permanent damage. Changing stiffness also changes the numerical scale used in the energy-like display,so redness is not a fair cross-setting absolute measure.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Keep a common colour scale across stiffness settings,or let the visitor choose a new observation such as recovery time.

rooms.question: Can a pattern form without anybody drawing its outline?
rooms.ontology: A reaction-diffusion system stores concentrations,local reactions and spatial exchange; a visible image reads one field.
rooms.action: Select a preset,watch patches develop,then move FEED slightly while keeping KILL fixed. Use RESET to begin a new run.
rooms.observable: Spots,stripes or connected regions change as the concentration field evolves; the image need not follow the hand directly.
rooms.mechanism: Each step computes uvv,subtracts/adds reaction terms,adds weighted neighbour Laplacian,feed andkill,clamps U/V0–1 and swaps buffers.
rooms.limit: Preset names describe a tendency,not a guaranteed biological form. Reset seeding and elapsed evolution also affect the picture.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Keep a seed and initial field fixed across paired feed settings; let one visitor disturb a region and another decide what counts as the same pattern.
rooms.cautions: Source read only; actual museum runtime, reachability, controls and learner understanding remain unverified.

rooms.question: Which openings connect inside a surface that seems to fold through itself?
rooms.ontology: An implicit surface is selected from a scalar field by a threshold; its geometry can change when field parameters change.
rooms.action: Follow an opening with your eye,then move to another viewpoint to test whether two apparent passages connect.
rooms.observable: The current specimen is a gyroid-like porous structure with noise perturbation.
rooms.mechanism: S linearly maps tofrequency,noise amplitude andthreshold; GyroidFieldGenerator samples sin(kx)cos(ky)+sin(ky)cos(kz)+sin(kz)cos(kx) plusnoise and builds a marching-cubes mesh.
rooms.limit: S is an authored morphing control,not measured thermodynamic entropy. One frozen specimen cannot show the effect of changing three coupled parameters.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Compare fixed-seed specimens varying only threshold,then onlyfrequency,before offering a combined morphing axis.
rooms.cautions: Source read only; actual museum runtime, reachability, controls and learner understanding remain unverified. No visitorS slider; static source-supported encounter prepares isosurfaces without presenting entropy metaphor as physics.
